references.title: Labour Code 45/2019/QH14 art.98(1)(a): an employee who works overtime on a normal day is paid at least 150% of the wage of the normal working hour.

Decree 145/2020/NĐ-CP arts.54(1)(a3)–(a4), 55(1)(a): the monthly wage is divided by the normal working days of the month the enterprise chose and the day wage by the normal hours of the day; the overtime hour wage is the month’s wage for the work divided by the month’s actual normal hours. The hourly base is the contractual rate plus the contract’s FIXED_ALLOWANCE job-related allowances; meal, housing, insurance-equivalent and work-expense allowances, bonuses, and overtime, night and holiday pay stay out.

conversion:
const entry = get(ctx, 'entry', {});
return ctx.hour_rate * Number(get(entry, 'quantity', 0)) * ctx.lookup.multiplier;
description: Normal working-day overtime hours, paid at the statutory multiplier.

references.title: Labour Code 45/2019/QH14 art.98(1)(b): work on a weekly rest day is paid at least 200%; every hour worked on that day is overtime. A public holiday falling on a rest day is paid as a holiday (Decree 145/2020/NĐ-CP art.55(3)). The hourly base is the same as OVERTIME.

references.title: Labour Code 45/2019/QH14 art.98(1)(c): work on a public holiday or paid day off is paid at least 300% for each hour worked, excluding the holiday pay a monthly wage already carries; hours banked as time off are not worked hours. The hourly base is the same as OVERTIME.

references.title: Labour Code 45/2019/QH14 arts.98(2), 106: work between 22:00 and 06:00 is night work and is paid at least 30% above the normal-day hour wage for each night hour, whether the hour is normal or overtime (Decree 145/2020/NĐ-CP art.56(1); art.57 adds the night-overtime supplement). The hourly base is the same as OVERTIME.

Decree 145/2020/NĐ-CP arts.54(1)(a3)–(a4), 55(1)(a): the monthly wage is divided by the normal working days of the month the enterprise chose and the day wage by the normal hours of the day; the overtime hour wage is the month’s wage for the work divided by the month’s actual normal hours. The hourly base is the contractual rate plus the contract’s FIXED_ALLOWANCE job-related allowances; meal, housing, insurance-equivalent and work-expense allowances, bonuses, and overtime, night and holiday pay stay out.
Circular 111/2013/TT-BTC art.3(1)(i) exempts the night-work premium from personal income tax to 2025; Law 109/2025 art.4(8) from 2026. This is a tax treatment of the premium, not a pay rate.

references.title: Labour Code 45/2019/QH14 art.98(3); Decree 145/2020/NĐ-CP art.57(1)(b): overtime at night adds 20% of the daytime hour wage of that day — 100% on a normal day with no daytime overtime, 150% where the day also has daytime overtime, 200% on a weekly rest day and 300% on a public holiday. The admitted night-overtime hours carry their day kind; lookup.day_wage_factor holds those four statutory factors. On a public holiday every paid night hour of the holiday is in the supplement; on a normal or rest day only the night hours inside the overtime span are. The hourly base is the same as OVERTIME.
